title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-01-31

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a quirky early‑1970 show that turned a busted amp into an unforgettable acoustic set with standout Pigpen country/bluegrass numbers.
ai_review.review: Despite Phil’s amp blowing and a missing second electric set, the band rolled with it, delivering a unique acoustic segment and several high‑energy country‑blues cuts that Deadheads rave about. The soundboard source is crisp and clear, making this off‑the‑cuff performance a must‑listen snapshot of the early Dead era.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple 4–5 star reviews praise both the musical moments and the recording quality; weighting favors a strong show with an excellent soundboard source.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers call the recording "TOPS" and note clear capture of banter and stage ambience; no major drop‑outs reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert pivots around an impromptu acoustic set after Phil’s amp failure, delivering a mix of country‑blues numbers that give the early show a distinctive, off‑the‑cuff character.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned for his bluegrass lead on Little Sadie and overall solid playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass/amp blew after the first set, forcing the acoustic segment.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for vocal leads on Long Black Limousine, Seasons of the Heart, Saw Mill, and other country‑styled songs.
